title: ALPHA YY
canon: Written by Mike Diaz in prison, mailed page by page to Marco Caruso (typed 2007, revised in pen 2009). Late-2000s New York — Staten Island and Manhattan's Little Italy: Mike and Dario, enforcers working a loan shark's list of beatings, collections and the odd hit, singing along to the car radio between bodies. An unsanctioned prison-kite job in New Jersey puts Mike's name in the air upstairs, and it is his oldest friend Marco who comes to the door: doorbell, 'Everything's gonna be alright now,' fade out.
look: Mid-2000s New York shot like the American crime pictures it descends from — 35mm, natural grain, muted unglamorous color. Most of the violence happens in flat ordinary daylight: overcast Staten Island streets, plastic-sheeted basements under a bare work bulb, Little Italy awnings under a white sky. Nights are practical-lit only — sodium streetlamps, cafe tungsten, restaurant neon, a porch bulb. The frame stays banal and everyday; the menace is in what the ordinary light falls on.
note: Six frames chosen from the v3 canon fold (the only substantive source: 03-setting, 07-locations and 09-visuals vault docs are empty stubs; character physicals from the series-overview syno and the canon text). Chosen: the opening Verrazzano crossing, the Little Italy double-park, the plastic-sheeted basement, Big Trouble at the cafe, the Chinatown cellar summons, and the sacred ending at Mike's door — the frames a poster or hero would use, three day / three night, both boroughs. Period pinned late-2000s by the ten-dollar-toll line. CAST CONTINUITY WARNING: the real Mike Diaz refs (Mike.jpg, magicPrison.jpg) show a shaved-bald, stocky man — canon's witness calls him 'the bald one' — but every earlier AI still renders Mike full-haired; those are off-model and should not seed regen. Argentinian.jpg is presumed the Big Trouble likeness and housie-mousie.jpg is an unconfirmed likeness (John? Marco?) — Marco to confirm both; housie-mousie.jpg is used nowhere. Marco's face is never held in any prompt (no confirmed ref), so the ending frames him from behind. — 2026-07-16 STORY-WAVE ADDITION (Story Law, Marco's ruling of this date): six frames appended, existing six untouched. Every new frame shows the work they do and what it costs — a clean 21:9 4K regeneration of the canonical 01-hero tower-catwalk frame (source alpha-yy-hero-1.png is only 2752x1536 and carries a Gemini sparkle watermark bottom-right that must NOT survive; it lives in 01-hero not 02-stills, so it is not reffed — the composition is carried fully in the prompt and only cast faces are reffed), plus the kite decoded by Father Bobby (the summons), the New Jersey kitchen with the dropped Glock (the job that dooms him, canon A7/A8), the dumpster disposal off the open trunk (the drive and the cleanup), Jimmy Chin's envelope in the basement den (the payment), and Marco walking away from Mike's door at two in the morning (the silence after — from behind per the no-Marco-ref rule). All beats mined from alpha-yy-canon-v3-feature.md.

stills.notes: Ref carries the real geography — Fort Wadsworth's stone battery under the bridge and the Narrows looking back at the harbor. Prompt owns the composition; avoids the generic-suspension-bridge failure and the off-canon ferry motif of earlier renders.
stills.prompt: High aerial view of the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge, New York, 2008 — the double-decked grey suspension span crossing from Brooklyn to Staten Island, the old stone casemates of Fort Wadsworth on the far shore, lower Manhattan a pale haze far up the harbor. Late morning under a flat overcast white sky; the only light is even grey daylight off the water, no sun, no shadows to speak of. Mid-span in thin traffic, one dark late-nineties American sedan heads for Staten Island, small in the frame — two men inside on their way to work, and the work ends with a body in the trunk. Grey-green water moving far below. Wide anamorphic composition, shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime cinema, muted color, natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: Mulberry Street, Little Italy, Manhattan, 2008, mid-morning. Shop awnings in red, white and green, fruit stands stacked to the sidewalk edge, a sanitation truck dead in the lane. A dark American sedan sits double-parked square in the street and nobody honks twice. Outside a social club, a row of old men with espresso and cigarettes track the car with their eyes the way the neighborhood tracks everything; a butcher in a bloody apron hauls a side of beef past a priest on the corner. The light is flat overcast daylight bouncing off the awnings and wet asphalt, with a faint warm tungsten glow from the cafe windows where espresso machines hiss. Eye-level from across the street, deep down the block. Wide anamorphic composition, shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime cinema, muted color, natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Refs hold the two faces and Mike's real build — shaved-bald, stocky, tank-top-and-open-shirt wardrobe per the prison photos. Fixes the full-haired off-model Mike of every earlier AI basement render. Menace by implication: plastic and a lowered pistol, no gore.
stills.prompt: Unfinished basement of a Staten Island rowhouse, 2008. Bare concrete floor, exposed joists, every wall hung with clear plastic sheeting that catches the light in dull folds — the room is dressed for something and it is not painting. The only light is one bare incandescent work bulb hanging from the ceiling and a weak grey stab of daylight through a small ground-level hopper window; everything beyond the bulb's throw falls to black. A stocky, shaved-bald man in an open button-up shirt over a white tank stands at ease with a pistol held loose at his side, cigarette in his lips, unbothered; his leaner dark-haired partner shuts the door to the outside. Shadows hard and close, tungsten-warm against the cold window light. Wide anamorphic composition, shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime cinema, muted color, natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: Sidewalk tables outside a small East Village cafe on Avenue A, New York, 2008, night. A stocky, shaved-bald man in an open button-up shirt leans in close to whisper to a beautiful dark-haired young woman in a leather jacket; she is reading him, half a smile, not giving him anything yet. Espresso cups and biscotti on the little table, her friends laughing soft-focus at the next one. The light is all practical: warm tungsten spilling from the cafe windows behind them, a green-white streetlamp filtering through the park trees across the avenue, the ember of his cigarette; the street beyond falls off into darkness and parked cars. Intimate two-shot at table height, shallow focus. Wide anamorphic composition, shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime cinema, muted color, natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Refs hold both leads' faces at mid-distance; body armor under civilian shirts per the gearing-up montage. The glowing sidewalk cellar doors are the summons itself — 'it's just the b-a-s-e-m-e-n-t.' Avoids generic-triad-neon by keeping the light sourced: neon, sodium, stairwell.
stills.prompt: A narrow Chinatown street off Canal, Manhattan, 2008, late night after the restaurants close. Steel sidewalk cellar doors stand open in front of a shuttered restaurant, hard yellow light rising out of the stairwell below and catching the steam from a grate; two guards stand flanking the opening, casual jackets, hands loose. Approaching from the curb, a stocky shaved-bald man and his leaner dark-haired partner, both bulked slightly by vests under ordinary shirts, cigarettes lit. The light is all practical: red and green restaurant neon reflected in the wet street, one orange sodium streetlamp overhead, the glow climbing out of the cellar — no other source. Ducts, fire escapes and hanging signs vanish into darkness above. Wide anamorphic composition, shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime cinema, muted color, natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: The sacred ending — the frame the whole property is for. Refs hold Mike stripped to boxers and tank, a mortal everyday man; the visitor in black is framed from behind because no confirmed Marco likeness exists (housie-mousie.jpg unruled). No gunfire shown: the doorbell moment, not the shots.
stills.prompt: Front step of a modest vinyl-sided Staten Island house, 2008, two in the morning, the street dead quiet. The front door has just opened. Inside, a stocky, shaved-bald man stripped to boxers and a white tank top — a very mortal, everyday man, a small plate of food going cold on the coffee table behind him — stands in the doorway. On the step, seen from behind over his shoulder, a broad man dressed entirely in black, still, unhurried, an old friend's ease in his stance. The only light: the bare porch bulb over the door, the blue flicker of a television from the living room, and one orange sodium streetlamp far down the block of parked cars; the yard between holds full dark. Shot from the darkness of the front yard, the lit doorway framing them both. Wide anamorphic composition, shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime cinema, muted color, natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: Top of a main tower of the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge, New York, 2008, dusk just after sundown. On the steel maintenance catwalk between the cable saddles, two men stand nearly back to back, unhurried, a hundred stories over the Narrows. The stocky one in a dark baseball cap and dark work jacket draws on a cigarette, smoke curling, hand in pocket; his leaner dark-haired partner in a dark zip jacket faces the other way along the catwalk, a black pistol still hanging loose in his right hand. At their feet on the checker-plate deck: a dark plastic tarp streaked with blood, coils of white utility rope, slack rigging straps — the job is done and not yet cleaned up. Behind the smoker, the lit skyline of lower Manhattan far up the harbor under a burnt-orange afterglow; on the other side, the great suspension cables and vertical suspender ropes sweep down to the double-deck roadway far below, streams of white headlights and red taillights crossing to Staten Island. The only light: the dying orange sky, the city and roadway lights below, and the cigarette ember — no other source, faces mostly in silhouette. Clean 21:9 widescreen, 4K. Wide anamorphic composition, shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime cinema, muted color, natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark, no logo.

stills.notes: The summons — canon: Father Bobby deciphers the prison kite in his office over counted money and scotch (v3 feature, Father Bobby office scene). The priest has no ref; the prompt owns him — early fifties, ex-con heaviness under the collar. Stranger test: a priest decoding a smuggled letter for cash while two heavies wait on the words.
stills.prompt: A parish priest's back office in a Roman Catholic church rectory, Little Italy, Manhattan, 2008, mid-afternoon. At a scarred oak desk, a heavy-set priest in his early fifties — Roman collar, ex-con's thick hands and boxer's nose — leans over a creased sheet of prison-kite paper covered edge to edge in miniature coded handwriting, working it out line by line onto a notepad. At his elbow: a short stack of counted twenties, three poured glasses of scotch, the bottle open. Across the desk a stocky, shaved-bald man in an open button-up over a white tank watches the priest's pen, and his leaner dark-haired partner stands behind the chair, arms folded. The light is weak grey daylight through a frosted leaded window and one warm green-shaded desk lamp pooled on the kite and the money; crucifix and file cabinets fall off into shadow. Eye-level across the desk, the letter and the cash sharp in the pool of lamplight. Wide anamorphic composition, shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime cinema, muted color, natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: The job that dooms him — canon A7/A8: the unsanctioned Jersey hit, the brand-new Glock tossed on the body, Dario stopped with the coffee cup, Mike already walking. The stake in the frame is the gun being left behind. Violence by aftermath, not gore — one still figure, the pistol on his chest, flat ordinary daylight per the look.
stills.prompt: Kitchen of a suburban tract house in northern New Jersey, 2008, mid-morning, flat white overcast daylight through the window over the sink — ordinary light on an ordinary room. A drip coffee maker mid-brew on the counter, steam rising, cabinets half open. On the linoleum floor a big fair-haired man in a t-shirt lies still on his back, and resting squarely on his chest sits a brand-new black pistol, left there on purpose. A stocky, shaved-bald man in an open button-up over a white tank is already walking out the back door, done, not looking back; his leaner dark-haired partner stands frozen mid-room with a mug of fresh coffee halfway to his mouth, eyes down on the gun on the dead man's chest, knowing it is a mistake. No gore beyond a thin dark line along the floor seam; the horror is how ordinary the kitchen stays. Eye-level from the doorway, the gun on the chest sharp in the foreground third. Wide anamorphic composition, shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime cinema, muted color, natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: The drive and the cleanup — canon Ep I: the boys empty garbage bags of Alan's pieces into a dumpster off the car while Mike sings along to Bob Marley. The story lives in the open trunk feeding the dumpster and in Mike singing while he does it. Daylight banality per the look; contents stay bagged, no gore.
stills.prompt: A dead-end service alley behind a row of brick storefronts, Staten Island, New York, 2008, midday under a flat white overcast sky — even grey light, no shadows. A dark late-nineties American sedan is backed up tight to a rusted green municipal dumpster, trunk lid up. A stocky, shaved-bald man in an open button-up over a white tank swings a heavy, sagging black garbage bag up over the dumpster lip one-handed, mouth open mid-song, entirely at ease; his leaner dark-haired partner hands the next taut heavy bag out of the trunk, where two more wait on a plastic liner. Weeds in the fence line, a stack of wet cardboard, one gull on the dumpster's far corner; nobody else in the alley and the backs of the buildings have no windows that care. The bags hang with a weight that is not garbage. Eye-level from down the alley, the open trunk and the dumpster in one line. Wide anamorphic composition, shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime cinema, muted color, natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: The payment — canon: Jimmy Chin's subterranean den, antique desk, Chinese artwork, the bowing servant passing the envelope to Mike under a room full of guns. Jimmy has no ref; the prompt owns him — young, immaculate white silk gi, big smile. Stranger test: money changing hands in a guarded basement, everyone armed, the smile doing the threatening.
stills.prompt: A sub-basement den beneath a Chinese restaurant off Canal Street, Manhattan, 2008, night. A moderate windowless underground office grounded by a large antique blackwood desk, walls hung with Chinese scroll paintings, a carved lacquer screen, shelves of porcelain. Behind the desk stands a young man in an immaculate white silk gi, arms wide, a big host's smile; before it, a bowing servant extends a thick paper envelope with both hands to a stocky, shaved-bald man in an open button-up over a white tank, who takes it without smiling; his leaner dark-haired partner stands close at his shoulder, jacket open, hand not far from his waistband. Along the walls, armed men in dark casual jackets stand half-swallowed by shadow, shapes more than faces. The light is all practical: a green-shaded banker's lamp on the desk, two red paper lanterns overhead, a bare bulb over the stairwell door — warm pools in a dark room, the envelope catching the lamplight at center. Eye-level past the servant's bow. Wide anamorphic composition, shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime cinema, muted color, natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: The silence after — the reverse of the sacred ending: the man in black leaving Mike's door at two in the morning, door standing open behind him, nobody in it. No refs: Marco's face is never held (no confirmed likeness; housie-mousie.jpg unruled), and he is framed walking away. Stranger test: an open door, a lit empty doorway, a man in black already halfway down the block.
stills.prompt: A block of modest vinyl-sided houses on a dead-quiet Staten Island street, 2008, two in the morning. From low across the street: a broad man dressed entirely in black walks away down the sidewalk between parked cars, back to camera, unhurried, hands empty at his sides. Behind him, one small house stands with its bare porch bulb still burning and the front door standing wide open — warm hallway light and the blue flicker of a television spilling onto the empty step, and no one in the doorway. The only other light is a single orange sodium streetlamp far down the row of parked cars; every other window on the block is dark. The open door and the walking man tell the whole thing: something final just happened in that house and the street will never say so. Wide anamorphic composition, shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime cinema, muted color, natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.
